items.headline: Bitcoin Core changes security rules as AI makes finding code bugs dangerously easy

confirmed_facts.text: Bitcoin Core changes security rules as AI makes finding code bugs dangerously easy Developers merged a policy change that ends the months-long embargo for flaws a chatbot could rediscover, after a summer in which AI found hundreds of bitcoin bugs before the humans did.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Bitcoin Core changes security rules as AI makes finding code bugs dangerously easy Developers merged a policy change that ends the months-long embargo for flaws a chatbot could rediscover, after a summer in which AI found hundreds of bitcoin bugs before the humans did.

confirmed_facts.text: - Maintainers said the change would speed fixes for easily rediscovered flaws, though updates may receive less testing before reaching users.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: - Maintainers said the change would speed fixes for easily rediscovered flaws, though updates may receive less testing before reaching users.

confirmed_facts.text: - The policy follows a surge in AI-assisted security reports, including a review of 390 Bitcoin projects that identified 4,962 potential flaws, 85 of them critical.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: - The policy follows a surge in AI-assisted security reports, including a review of 390 Bitcoin projects that identified 4,962 potential flaws, 85 of them critical.

confirmed_facts.text: Bitcoin Core, the software most of the bitcoin network runs on, will stop sitting on bug fixes for months when the bug is one an AI could find again, after its maintainers merged a change to the project’s security policy on Thursday.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Bitcoin Core, the software most of the bitcoin network runs on, will stop sitting on bug fixes for months when the bug is one an AI could find again, after its maintainers merged a change to the project’s security policy on Thursday.

confirmed_facts.text: The logic was that shipping a fix quietly and explaining it much later kept attackers from learning about a hole before the people running nodes, the computers that check and relay every bitcoin transaction, had upgraded.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: The logic was that shipping a fix quietly and explaining it much later kept attackers from learning about a hole before the people running nodes, the computers that check and relay every bitcoin transaction, had upgraded.

confirmed_facts.text: But the old rule was built for a world where finding a bug took skill, and the spread of AI tools has broken how that process worked.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: But the old rule was built for a world where finding a bug took skill, and the spread of AI tools has broken how that process worked.
